posts.title: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
posts.summary: As a California state senator, Scott Wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI. Now, after winning a tight congressional race for former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat, he could play a key role in setting federal AI policy.  I spoke with Wiener on Friday, only a…
bullets: California state senator Scott Wiener, who authored the vetoed SB 1047, is set to influence federal AI policy following his election to Congress.
Wiener is prioritizing the regulation of 'recursive self-improvement' in AI models, citing recent reports as evidence that current development speeds pose existential risks.
Despite receiving campaign funding from Anthropic-backed nonprofits, Wiener maintains a legislative record of pushing for AI oversight that often conflicts with Big Tech interests.

posts.title: The Download: empty AI climate claims, and an Nvidia investigation
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Opinion: The climate case for AI has not been made  —By Mary Nichols, distinguished counsel at the UCLA School of Law and the former chair of the California Air Resources Board,…
bullets: Nvidia shares fell 5% in pre-market trading following reports that CEO Jensen Huang is under investigation regarding a personal relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
Congressional Democrats are reportedly preparing a series of antitrust and regulatory investigations targeting major technology firms, including Apple and Meta.
Experts argue that current corporate claims regarding AI's potential to mitigate climate change lack empirical evidence and meaningful implementation in high-impact sectors.

posts.title: Jensen Huang’s Affair, The Culper Report, Huang’s Righteousness
posts.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a Chinese spy, and that might not be the end of his troubles. I hope he survives, but his influence will never be the same.
bullets: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has publicly admitted to an affair with a Chinese intelligence operative, creating a significant geopolitical and corporate governance crisis.
The revelation threatens to permanently diminish Huang's influence and standing, potentially destabilizing the leadership of the world's most critical AI hardware company.
The situation introduces severe regulatory and national security risks for Nvidia, given the company's central role in the global semiconductor supply chain and its complex relationship with China.
Investors must now weigh the potential for leadership transition or increased government scrutiny against the company's current market dominance.

posts.title: The Optical Superhighway For AI
posts.summary:
Exponentially increasing AI compute performance requires exponential interconnect speeds.
The post The Optical Superhighway For AI appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The industry is transitioning from copper to optical interconnects to support the exponential bandwidth requirements of AI scale-up and scale-out architectures.
The OCI-MSA consortium, featuring major players like Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, and Microsoft, aims to standardize interoperable optical interconnects to replace power-hungry pluggable transceivers.
The roadmap for optical interconnects involves moving from current pluggable solutions toward near-packaged optics (NPO) and eventually co-packaged optics (CPO) to reduce power and cost.
The OCI-MSA Gen 1 specification utilizes multi-wavelength, bidirectional signaling to increase data density per fiber, addressing the physical limitations of traditional copper-based interconnects.

posts.title: China October NEV retail sales fall 13.7% as penetration hits record 67.5%, CPCA data shows
posts.summary:
China's NEV retail sales totaled 1.109 million units in October, marking the 10th consecutive month of year-on-year decline.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's NEV retail sales fell 13.7% year-on-year in October to 1.109 million units, marking the tenth consecutive month of annual decline.
Despite domestic retail weakness, NEV exports surged 144.7% to 582,000 units, providing a critical buffer for wholesale performance.
NEV penetration reached a record 67.5% of total passenger vehicle retail sales, as high oil prices continue to drive consumer migration away from gasoline vehicles.
